mechanism.description: Treatment-response interaction claim: Patients with preserved consciousness (GCS 1315) are more likely to obtain net benefit from IV alteplase because preserved GCS typically indicates smaller core and higher chance of functional recovery; patients with deep reduced consciousness (GCS ≤8) generally derive less benefit or may be harmed due to large established infarct, mass effect, or high sICH risk. The interaction is moderated by stroke location — posterior circulation strokes may present with low GCS yet still have salvageable tissue and hence may not follow this pattern.

Treatment-response interaction claim (conditional): If IST-3 applied a fixed maximum alteplase dose (e.g., 90 mg), very high-weight patients who were dose-capped may have lower mg/kg exposure and therefore reduced recanalization probability and smaller net functional benefit; low-weight patients may receive higher mg/kg and thus higher efficacy but also greater hemorrhagic risk. The net effect direction depends on whether reduced mg/kg leads to clinically meaningful reductions in recanalization that outweigh any reduction in bleeding.
